rows.speaker: المعترضون
rows.claim: The objection says both camps hold souls survive bodily separation and are distinguished by accidents; for potential souls, attachment to different bodies may itself individuate them.
rows.anchor: أن الأرواح عند الفريقين باقية بعد المفارقة ولا يكون تمايزها بالماهية ولوازمها بل بالعوارض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a soul divided, its parts would differ from the whole; essential difference makes the parts already distinct, while nonessential difference requires unequal magnitude and thus divisibility.
rows.anchor: كل ما انقسم وجب أن يكون جزؤه مخالفا لكله ضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even granting that an immaterial simple soul cannot split after unity, the individual determinations arise only after bodily attachment, so each soul is originated as an individual.
rows.anchor: تعين كل واحدة من تلك النفوس من حيث هي حادثا وهو المطلوب

rows.speaker: المعترضون
rows.claim: An objection asks why distinction must depend on a qualifying attribute; Alusi answers by the same reasoning used for individuation itself.
rows.anchor: الإمتياز لا يوجد إلا عند الإختصاص بوصف

rows.speaker: المعترضون
rows.claim: An objection proposes that souls differ through constitutive qualities; Alusi says it is not self-evident that each soul-kind must have several individuals, and one individual per kind would complete the argument.
rows.anchor: إن النفوس لا يجوز أن تتمايز بالصفات المقومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument does not depend on disproving transmigration: plurality within one species shows individuality is not essential, but caused by relation to a particular body, so the soul is not individuated before that body.
rows.anchor: ليس كذلك لأنا إذا وجدنا من النوع الواحد شخصين علمنا أن تلك الشخصية ليست معولة لتلك الماهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An inhering accident cannot distinguish a soul, since its inherence presupposes the soul is already distinguished; individuation must depend on the receptacle or body, while theologians also reject such accounts by infinite regress.
rows.anchor: تلك العلة لا يمكن أن تكون حالة فيها لأن ذلك متوقف على امتيازها عن غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Potential souls first become distinct through attachment to particular receptacles; each then becomes aware of its own self, and that awareness persists, preserving distinction.
rows.anchor: النفوس الهيولانية يتميز بعضها عن البعض أولا بسبب تعلقها بالقابل المعين ثم أنه يلزم من تعين كل واحد منها شعورها بذاتها الخاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before bodies, a soul could not be distinct: awareness follows distinction, and no other distinguisher exists to precede that awareness.
rows.anchor: لو تميزت لكان المميز سوى الشعور حتى يترتب هو عليه وقد بين أنه ليس هناك مميز

rows.speaker: صاحب المعتبر
rows.claim: The author of al-Muʿtabar argues that prebodily souls either transmigrated from earlier bodies, which we would remember, or were idle in nature; Alusi calls the whole argument very weak.
rows.anchor: استدل صاحب المعتبر على حدوثها بأنها لو كانت موجودة قبل الأبدان

rows.speaker: قدماء الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Ancient philosophers argue that anything originated needs matter to make existence preferable to nonexistence; thus an originated soul would be material, which they deny.
rows.anchor: كل ما يحدث فلا بد أن يكون له مادة تكون سببا لأن يصير أولى بالوجود

rows.speaker: قدماء الفلاسفة
rows.claim: They argue that if souls began with bodies, infinitely many past bodies would entail infinitely many current souls, impossible because whatever admits increase and decrease is finite.
rows.anchor: الثاني أنها لو كانت حادثة لكان حدوثها لحدوث الأبدان لكن الأبدان الماضية غير متناهية

rows.speaker: قدماء الفلاسفة
rows.claim: They argue that originated things perish, whereas souls are everlasting by consensus, so souls must be eternal.
rows.anchor: أنها لو لم تكن أزلية لم تكن أبدية لما ثبت أن كل كائن فاسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi accepts that souls depend for origination on bodies, but rejects the inference that dependence means they are bodily inhering in them.
rows.anchor: ويرد عليهم أنه أريد بكونها مادية أن حدوثها يكون متوقفا على حدوث البدن فالأمر كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that finite souls follow from their ability to increase or decrease is not self-evident and requires proof; the argument works only for things capable of bodily extension or inherence.
rows.anchor: المقدمة القائلة إن كل قابل للزيادة والنقصان متناه ليست من الأوليات قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The philosophers give no proof for the premise that whatever is not eternal cannot be everlasting, so that premise is not accepted.
rows.anchor: قضية لا حجة لهم على تصحيحها فلا تقبل

rows.speaker: الغزالي والشيخ من الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali and the philosopher called the Shaykh hold souls are one species; Alusi says the Shaykh offered not even a doubt, much less a proof.
rows.anchor: صرح به جماعة من المتكلمين كالغزالي وغيره وإليه ذهب الشيخ من الفلاسفة إلا أنه لم يأت لذلك بشبهة

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another proponent argues that if human souls share their nature yet differ by an essential constituent, they would be composite and therefore bodily.
rows.anchor: أن النفوس مشتركة في أنها نفوس بشرية فلو انفصل بعضها عن بعض بمقوم ذاتي

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: A second argument for one soul-species says all people share capacities for knowledge and moral traits; since souls are known as perceiving and volitionally active, they are equal in all intelligible attributes.
rows.anchor: الثاني أنا نرى الناس مشتركين في صحة العلم بالمعلومات وفي صحة التخلق بالأخلاق

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: A third argument says every immaterial essence knows itself; Zayd's soul apprehends only an essence capable of cognition and volition, shared by all souls, so their full essence is one species.
rows.anchor: نفس زيد مثلا مجردة فهي عاقلة لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects the first argument: souls might differ in species without sharing a genus, or share features as nonconstitutive concomitants; even essential composition need not be bodily.
rows.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن هذه النفوس وإن كانت مختلفة بالنوع فهي غير متشاركة في الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second same-species argument rests on inadequate induction: one cannot show every person receives every intelligible, or that a soul able to receive one attribute receives all attributes.
rows.anchor: وأما الثاني فمداره الإستقراء ويضعف ذلك لوجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third argument would make all separate beings one species, which Alusi says is untenable.
rows.anchor: يقتضي أن يكون جميع المفارقات نوعا واحدا وهو مما لا سبيل إليه

rows.speaker: شرذمة وصاحب المعتبر
rows.claim: A small group holds that souls differ by species, and this is the position of the author of al-Muʿtabar.
rows.anchor: وذهب شرذمة إلى اختلافها بالنوع وهذا المعتبر عند صاحب المعتبر

rows.speaker: صاحب المعتبر
rows.claim: The best case for differing soul-species points to differences in knowledge, strength, anger, and forbearance despite similar temperaments, and prophetic power over universal matter not caused by temperament.
rows.anchor: أحسن ما عول عليه في الإستدلال له اختلاف الناس في العلم والجهل والقوة والضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the argument from personal differences and prophetic power is not a proof, only weak persuasion.
rows.anchor: ليس في الحقيقة من البراهين بل هو من الإقناعات الضعيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit's true nature is difficult to know; God made it a great sign of divine majesty and perfection.
rows.anchor: أن الوقوف على حقيقة الروح أمر عسر والطويل إليه وعر وقد جعل الله سبحانه ذاك من أعظم آياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' prostration to Adam may have been homage and honor, or prostration to God with Adam as the qibla where divine power's marvels appeared; Alusi cites Hassan's line about praying toward the qibla.
rows.anchor: على وجه التحية والتعظيم أو لله تعالى وهو عليه السلام بمنزلة القبلة حيث ظهرت فيه تعاجيب آثار قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fall down indicates actual prostration in its ordinary sense, not merely bowing as some suggested.
rows.anchor: في أمرهم بالوقوع أي السقوط دليل على أن ليس المأمور به مجرد الإنحناء كما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creator is God, who makes the wondrous things just listed or whatever He wills; the noncreator makes nothing, great or small. The comparison rebukes idolatry by denying any likeness between God and idols.
rows.anchor: ما ذكر من المخلوقات البديعة أو يخلق كل شيء يريده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ after the interrogative hamza directs the denial to the supposed inference of likeness from God's preceding mighty acts.
rows.anchor: وتعقيب الهمزة بالفاء لتوجيه الإنكار إلى ترتب توهم المشابهة المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is singled out from the preceding acts because it is their greatest and clearest instance, or because each preceding act is itself a particular creation.
rows.anchor: والإقتصار على ذكر الخلق من بين ما تقدم لكونه أعظمه وأظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although one might expect the negative comparison first, the chosen order respects possession's precedence over absence and stresses that shirk lowers lordship to the level of inert matter.
rows.anchor: وكان حق الكلام بحسب الظاهر في باديء النظر أفمن لا يخلق كمن يخلق لكن قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noncreator may mean all noncreating beings, intelligent and inanimate, with من favoring rational beings; alternatives are intelligent beings alone with idols inferred a fortiori, or idols alone, but Alusi prefers the broader reading.
rows.anchor: والمراد بمن لا يخلق كل ما هذا شأنه من ذوي العلم كالملائكة وعيسى عليهم السلام وغيرهم كالأصنام

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Idols fall under the denial either directly or by an a-fortiori inference: if even intelligent noncreators are unlike God, inert idols are still less comparable.
rows.anchor: ودخول الأصنام في حكم عدم المشابهة إما بطريق الإندراج أو بطريق الإنفهام بدلالة النص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi notes that the verse is used to refute the Muʿtazilite doctrine that human beings create their own acts.
rows.anchor: واستدل بالآية على بطلان مذهب المعتزلة في زعمهم أن العباد خالقون لأفعالهم

rows.speaker: الشهاب
rows.claim: Al-Shihab allows the universal scope of creates to come from treating the verb as intransitive, and says the verse then cannot refute the Muʿtazilite claim that people create acts, since universal negation permits particular affirmation.
rows.anchor: وقال الشهاب بعد أن قرر تقدير المفعول عاما على طرز ما ذكرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi suspects the transmitted passage may be corrupt; otherwise he regards its denial of the verse's argument against the Muʿtazila as a lapse by al-Shihab.
rows.anchor: ولعلها سقيمة وإلا فلا أظن ذلك إلا كبوة جواد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase asks why people do not notice and recall what is already clear, needing only recollection of something previously conceived and then forgotten.
rows.anchor: أي ألا تلاحظون فلا تتذكرون ذلك فإنه لجلائه لا يحتاج إلى شيء سوى التذكر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some supply عدم المساواة as the omitted object of remember, then treat remember as an explicit metaphor for knowing because there was no earlier conception to recall.
rows.anchor: وقدر بعضهم المفعول عدم المساواة وذكر أنه لعدم سبقه حتى يتصور فيه حقيقة التذكر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account makes the metaphor explicit in the estimated object; another makes it implicit there and treats the assertion of remembering as its imaginative elaboration.
rows.anchor: الاستعارة مكنية في المفعول المقدر وإثبات التذكر تخييل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage begins showing that the worshipped gods are plainly unfit for worship; spelling out their obvious defects exposes the idolaters' folly.
rows.anchor: شروع في تحقيق أن آلهتهم بمعزل عن استحقاق العبادة وتوضيحه بحيث لا يبقى فيه شائبة ريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deities worshipped apart from God create absolutely nothing; creating anything is not among their attributes.
rows.anchor: الآلهة الذين تعبدونهم أيها الكفار

rows.speaker: بعض الأجلة
rows.claim: One explanation connects this to the preceding denial of likeness: since noncreators do not share in creating with the Creator, the conclusion that they are unlike Him follows without repetition.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض الأجلة أن ذكر هذا بعد نفي التشابه

rows.speaker: قيل عليه
rows.claim: An objection says the preceding reasoning already specifies God as creator and idols as noncreators, making the inference unnecessary; the repetition instead pairs with their being created.
rows.anchor: إنه مبني على أن من يخلق ومن لا مجرى على غير معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi answers that creator and noncreator are stated universally, though their contextual referents are God and idols; the earlier premise is so evident that it can still serve in the proof.
rows.anchor: المصرح به العموم في الموضعين وأما التخصيص فيهما بما ذكر فلأن من يخلق عندنا مخصوص به تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the better explanation for mentioning createdness is the pairing already indicated, rather than treating the repetition as redundant.
rows.anchor: ولعل الأوجه في توجيه الذكر ما أشرنا إليه أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noncreation alone does not entail createdness, so the verse states it explicitly: their possible natures depend on an agent for existence and continuance.
rows.anchor: وحيث أنه لا تلازم أصلا بين نفي الخالقية وبين المخلوقية أثبت ذلك لهم صريحا

rows.speaker: بعض الأجلة
rows.claim: The passive voice sharpens the contrast between the denied quality of creating and the affirmed quality of being created, while leaving the agent unstated because God is obvious.
rows.anchor: وبناء الفعل للمفعول كما قال بعض الأجلة لتحقيق التضاد والمقابلة بين ما أثبت لهم وما نفي عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun is placed first for emphasis, and both instances of creation retain their ordinary meaning.
rows.anchor: ولعل تقديم الضمير هنا لمجرد التقوى والمراد بالخلق منفيا ومثبتا المعنى المتبادر منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes the second creation as carving or shaping the idols, using rational language for them by treating them as rational and by rhetorical matching; applying this to the first creation is invalid because idol-making does not establish worthiness of worship.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يراد من الثاني النحت والتصوير بناء على أن المراد من الذين يدعونهم الأصنام

rows.speaker: الجمهور ومجاهد والأعرج وشيبة وأبو جعفر وهبيرة عن عاصم
rows.claim: The majority and the named readers read the surrounding verbs تسرون وتعلنون وتدعون with second-person tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بالتاء المثناة من فوق

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: In the well-known transmission from ʿĀṣim, the final تدعون is read with third-person yāʾ, while the first two verbs retain tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وفي المشهور عنه أنه قرأ بالياء آخر الحروف في الأخير وبالتاء في الأولين

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة
rows.claim: A transmission from Abu ʿAmr and Hamza reads all three surrounding verbs with third-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرئت الثلاثة بالياء في رواية عن أبي عمرو وحمزة

rows.speaker: الأعمش وطلحة
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Talha have explanatory variants with tāʾ in all three verbs; Alusi says these readings are interpretive because they diverge from the codex consonantal text.
rows.anchor: بالتاء من فوق في الأفعال الثلاث

rows.speaker: محمد اليماني
rows.claim: Muhammad al-Yamani reads يدعون in the passive, meaning the idols are summoned by the disbelievers and worshipped.
rows.anchor: بضم الياء وفتح العين مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that what people possess perishes explains why what is with God is better: worldly enjoyment, indeed the whole world, ends however abundant or long-lasting.
rows.anchor: تعليل للخيرية بطريق الإستئناف أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نفد with dāl means to run out or perish; نفذ with emphatic dhāl means to pass through, with a different vowel pattern.
rows.anchor: نفد بكسر العين ينفد بفتحها نفادا إذا ذهب وفنى وأما نفذ بالذال المعجمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is with God comprises the treasuries of His worldly and otherworldly mercy and does not expire; worldly blessings count among lasting good deeds because they connect to and lead to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: من خزائن رحمته الدنيوية والآخروية

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Ibn Jubayr that what is with God in both clauses means the reward of the afterlife; some leading authorities chose this interpretation.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن جبير أن المراد بما عند الله في الموضعين الثواب الأخروي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the nominal form بَاقٍ rather than a present-tense verb signals permanence.
rows.anchor: وفي إيثار الاسم على صيغة المضارع من الدلالة على الدوام ما لا يخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi uses the verse against Jahm ibn Safwan's claim that the bliss of Paradise ends.
rows.anchor: ورد بالآية على جهم بن صفوان حيث زعم أن نعيم الجنة منقطع

rows.speaker: عاصم وابن كثير
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ibn Kathir read the verb with first-person nūn, shifting from third-person reference to direct divine speech; the other canonical readers use yāʾ without that shift.
rows.anchor: بنون العظمة وهي قراءة عاصم وابن كثير على طريقة الالتفات من الغيبة إلى التكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward clause repeats the promise that God's reward is better, with oath-like emphasis to encourage steadfastness in the covenant.
rows.anchor: تكرير للوعد المستفاد من قوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who were patient are people steadfast in their covenant or enduring persecution by polytheists and the hardships of Islam, including keeping covenants despite threats of breach.
rows.anchor: على العهد أو على أذية المشركين ومشاق الإسلام التي من جملتها الوفاء بالعهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أجرهم is the direct object of لنجزين and means their particular reward corresponding to their patience.
rows.anchor: أي لنعطينهم أجرهم الخاص بهم بمقابلة صبرهم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan identifies the best deed as patience, an inward act needed for every obligation and thus the head of all works; the wording implies an omitted genitive, the reward of their patience.
rows.anchor: وهو الصبر فإنه من الأعمال القلبية والكلام على حذف مضاف أي لنجزينهم بجزاء صبرهم

rows.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
rows.claim: The genitive superlative emphasizes the reward's excellence, not that only the best of their works is rewarded; this reading encourages them and parallels the wording in 16:89.
rows.anchor: إنما أضيف الأحسن إلى ما ذكر للإشعار بكمال حسنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading promises each person, even for the lowest-ranked deed, the great reward otherwise given for the highest; it generously absorbs momentary distress into beautiful patience.
rows.anchor: لنعطينهم بمقابلة الفرد الأدنى من أعمالهم ما نعطيه بمقابلة الفرد الأعلى منها من الأجر الجزيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse makes أحسن an adjective of an omitted reward, with the genitive expressing comparison: God rewards them with a reward better than their deeds through multiplication.
rows.anchor: صفة جزاء محذوفا والإضافة على معنى من التفضيلية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes the best works as obligatory and recommended acts, or acts whose omission is also preferable, such as prohibited and disliked acts; neutral acts receive no reward. Al-Irshad rejects this as constricting mercy while exhorting good works.
rows.anchor: المراد بالأحسن ما ترجح فعله على تركه كالواجبات والمندوبات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the best is voluntary worship because it is chosen rather than imposed; reward for it entails reward for obligatory good works, but Alusi calls this interpretation entirely unsound.
rows.anchor: المراد بالأحسن النفل وكان أحسن لأنه لم يحتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is an independent consolation for the Prophet over the strain caused by the opponents: the Qur'an was not sent to burden him in dispute with obstinate leaders or in grief at their rejection, but to convey and remind; compare 18:6.
rows.anchor: عما كان يعتريه من جهد المشركين من التعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here شقاء means toil and distress, illustrated by the proverb about a colt trainer and a poem contrasting the rational person who suffers with the ignorant person who enjoys hardship.
rows.anchor: الشقاء شاسع في ذلك المعنى ومنه المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was not sent to exhaust himself through debate and excessive sorrow for their disbelief; he has delivered and reminded, so their refusal after that is no fault of his.
rows.anchor: بل لتبلغ وتذكر وقد فعلت فلا عليك أن لم يؤمنوا بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from Ali cited through Ibn Mardawayh is used for the alternative that the verse turns the Prophet away from excessive exertion in worship and harsh ascetic disciplines; he was sent with the tolerant, upright religion.
rows.anchor: كما سمعت فيما أخرج ابن مردويه عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجه أي ما أنزلناه عليك لتتعب بنهك نفسك

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil reports that Abu Jahl, al-Naḍr ibn al-Harith, and al-Muṭʿim told the Prophet, after seeing his worship, that abandoning their religion and receiving the Qur'an made him suffer; God denied their claim.
rows.anchor: أن أبا جهل والنظر بن الحرث والمطعم قالوا لرسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents may use شقاء literally as the opposite of happiness, while God's use echoes their wording by rhetorical matching.
rows.anchor: والشقاء في كلامهم يحتمل أن يكون بمعناه الحقيقي وهو ضد السعادة والتعبير به في كلامه تعالى من باب المشاكله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Ṭā Hā denotes the Qur'an, it may be nominative as the subject of the following sentence; repeating القرآن instead of a linking pronoun signals that the Qur'an is comforting mercy, not a cause of suffering.
rows.anchor: فيجوز فيه أن يكون محله الرفع على الأبتداء والجملة بعده خبره وقد أقيم فيها الظاهر أعنى القرآن مقام الضمير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other parses make the following clause predicate-less or the predicate of an omitted subject, treat Ṭā Hā as an object after an implied recite, or take it as an oath with its particle omitted.
rows.anchor: هو خبر لمبتدأ محذوف والجملة على القولين مستانفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Ṭā Hā is the Qur'an specifically meaning this sura, the following sentence can refer back to it; a general Qur'an reading also links through its inclusion of the sura.
rows.anchor: فالربط به لشموله للمبتدأ كما قيل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some reject taking Ṭā Hā to mean the sura because codices title it Sūrat Ṭā Hā, which they say creates the awkward construction like إنسان زيد; Alusi says this objection is plainly flawed.
rows.anchor: ومنع بعضهم إرادة السورة مطلقا لاتفاق المصاحف على ذكر سورة في العنوان مضافة إلى طه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some reject making the sura the subject when the next sentence is its predicate: denial of suffering presupposes earlier toil, which could not have resulted from revelation of this newly revealed sura; Alusi finds this objection reasonable.
rows.anchor: لأن نفي كون انزال القرآن للشقاء يستدعي وقوع الشقاء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: According to a report from Abu Jaʿfar, Ṭā Hā is one of the Prophet's names, so it is a vocative and the following sentence answers the call.
rows.anchor: يكون منادى وحكمه مشهور والجملة جواب النداء

rows.speaker: الحبر
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh from al-Ḥabr says Ṭā Hā is an oath by one of God's names, parsed accusative or genitive according to the oath construction.
rows.anchor: ما أخرج ابن منذر وابن مردويه عن الحبر من أنه قسم أقسم الله تعالى به وهو من أسمائه

rows.speaker: الأمير والربيع
rows.claim: Reports from the Commander of the Faithful and al-Rabiʿ treat Ṭā Hā as a verbal clause, after which the verse is an independent syntactic or explanatory sentence.
rows.anchor: وعلى ما روى عن الأمير كرم الله تعالى وجهه والربيع يكون جملة فعلية

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line إن على الله أن تبايعا illustrates the accusative construction after an implicit oath verb; another line, من وجه أشارت كليب بالأكف الأصابع, illustrates a genitive construction with an estimated oath particle.
rows.anchor: نظير قوله من وجه اشارت كليب بالاكف الأصابع

rows.speaker: طلحة
rows.claim: Talha reads ما نزل عليك القرآن with a doubled zāy and passive voice, making القرآن the subject of the verb.
rows.anchor: بتشديد الفعل وبناءئه للمفعول
